method: Three design agents proposed transports from different angles (one proposal was truncated before judging); two judge agents scored them under a failure-modes lens and a simplicity-and-security lens, running read-only git experiments against local bare repositories. Everything here is agent output kept as evidence for ADR-001; claims marked as experiments were run locally on macOS with git 2.39.5.

proposals.name: sb-git-transport: one state ref on the team's existing remote, hidden bare repo per remote per machine, worktree-less commits via index plumbing, one writer per (handle, machine) subtree, push-CAS with rebuild-on-reject, optional force-with-lease compaction
proposals.summary: Synchrobuilder publishes team state to a single ref on the team's existing git remote (default refs/heads/synchrobuilder-state; optional hidden refs/synchrobuilder/state once the host is verified). Each machine keeps a separate BARE git dir (no worktree, no remotes configured, templates and hooks disabled, gc.auto=0) under ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/repos/<remoteKey>/state.git, one per remote URL per machine, so the user's .git, index, refs and working tree are never read or written by the transport except for two read-only queries at session start (git common dir and the remote URL). Every commit is built without a worktree: fetch --depth=1 the ref into refs/sb/remote, read-tree that tip into a private temp index (GIT_INDEX_FILE passed only to the child git process), `git rm -r --cached` my own subtree state/<handle>/<machine>/, re-add my current local files with hash-object -w --stdin + update-index --cacheinfo, write-tree, commit-tree -p <tip>, push <commit>:<ref>. Because each writer only ever replaces its own subtree and regenerates it from local truth, a rejected push (another dev won the race) is resolved by simply fetching the new tip and rebuilding; no merge commits, no conflicts, linear history, verified with 5 concurrent publisher processes hammering one ref (55 commits, zero lost updates, zero merges). Compaction uses an orphan commit pushed with --force-with-lease=<ref>:<tip> (server-side CAS; a stale lease is rejected with 'stale info', verified), falling back to append-only when the host's policy blocks force pushes. A detached Node worker (spawned from SessionStart, single-flight per hidden repo) runs the 30-60 s loop with jittered backoff and immediate pushes on kicks, and writes an atomic snapshot.json that every hook reads (local file only, no git in hooks). Offline, missing remote, auth failure, force-push, ref deletion, shallow user clones and read-only collaborators all degrade to 'stale/local-only' with the exact status in the snapshot, never blocking Claude. The transport sits behind a small Transport interface (pull/publish/status) so a hosted hub can replace it later. All shipped code is Node ESM; git is spawned with an argv array, never a shell. Everything about git plumbing below was verified locally on git 2.39.5 / Node 24.16; everything about GitHub/GitLab/etc. behavior is listed under experiments_needed, not asserted.
proposals.mechanism:
LAYOUT ON THE REMOTE (one ref, one writer per file):
  <ref> = refs/heads/synchrobuilder-state (default) | refs/synchrobuilder/state (opt-in hidden namespace, see host_compatibility)
  tree:
    meta/schema.json                      # written once by whoever creates the ref: {"v":1}
    state/<handle>/<machine>/presence.json   # {v, handle, machine, sessions:[{sid8, branch, area, lastSeen, status}]}
    state/<handle>/<machine>/claims.json     # [{path, sid8, since, ttl}]
    state/<handle>/<machine>/tasks.json      # my task-board rows
    state/<handle>/<machine>/messages/<ulid>.json   # {to, text<=500, at, expires}  (written by SENDER)
    state/<handle>/<machine>/acks.json       # {seen:{<ulid>:at}}                  (written by RECIPIENT, so senders can prune)
    state/<handle>/<machine>/handoffs/<ulid>.json   # last 10 kept
    state/<handle>/<machine>/contracts.json  # [{path, commit, at}] shared-contract change alerts (paths + commit sha only, no diffs)
  Writer key = (handle, machine). handle from team.json/iam (brief); machine = first 8 hex of sha256(hostname + os user + a random salt persisted in ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}) so hostnames never leave the machine. Two machines of one developer, or two checkouts on one machine, therefore never share a file. Readers merge all subtrees.

LOCAL LAYOUT:
  ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/repos/<remoteKey>/state.git     # hidden BARE git dir (remoteKey = sha256 of normalized remote URL, 12 hex). CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA is exported to hook processes on every platform (hooks-core.md L116; experiments.md L107-L109) and survives plugin updates (plugins-reference.md L162-L163, L182); ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} changes on every update so nothing is written there (plugins-reference.md L174). Deleted on last-scope uninstall (plugins-reference.md L186), which is fine for a cache.
  ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/repos/<remoteKey>/snapshot.json  # merged read model for hooks, atomic tmp+rename
  ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/repos/<remoteKey>/worker.lock    # single-flight (mkdir-atomic), pid + heartbeat mtime
  ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/repos/<remoteKey>/sessions/<sid>.json, outbox/, kick, log/
  <git-common-dir>/synchrobuilder/link.json              # per checkout: {remoteKey, snapshotPath, handle, machine}; the ONLY thing hooks need to locate the snapshot. Written at SessionStart; hooks find it by walking up from the hook's cwd to .git (cwd follows worktrees while CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR does not: hooks-core.md L122, L372), reading the `.git` file/`commondir` file with fs only, no git spawn. Also holds mute flag (conflicts.md L144-L149).
  Fallback when CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA is absent (e.g. CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB, whose effect on CLAUDE_PLUGIN_* is 'not stated': monitors-tools-env.md L290, L368): use <git-common-dir>/synchrobuilder/ for everything (the brief's original location).

GIT RUNNER (shipped shape, verified in the experiment below):
  spawnSync('git', ['--git-dir='+H, '-c','commit.gpgsign=false', '-c','gc.auto=0', '-c','core.hooksPath='+H+'/nohooks', ...args], { env, cwd: H, input, encoding:'utf8', windowsHide:true, timeout })
  env = process.env minus {GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_NAMESPACE, GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES, GIT_PREFIX, GIT_EDITOR}, plus GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GCM_INTERACTIVE=never, SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never, GIT_AUTHOR/COMMITTER_NAME=<handle>, *_EMAIL=<handle>@synchrobuilder.invalid, and GIT_INDEX_FILE=<H>/sb-index ONLY on the index commands. The user's global/system git config (credential helpers, ssh config, url.insteadOf, proxies) is inherited on purpose; the user's repo-local config is not (see security_notes for the CI extraheader case). I hit the leak hazard myself during the experiment: exporting GIT_INDEX_FILE process-wide made `git status` in the user's clone fail with 'fatal: unable to read <blob>' because it read the hidden index. The runner therefore never mutates process.env.
  Hidden repo creation: git init -q --bare --template= <H>  (--template= skips init.templateDir hooks); then config gc.auto=0 (no background auto-gc, which matters on Windows), commit.gpgsign=false (commit-tree honors commit.gpgsign and a signing prompt would hang a background worker).
  Remote discovery (read-only, once per session, in the USER'S repo): git -C <cwd> rev-parse --git-common-dir; git -C <repo> ls-remote --get-url <remote> (applies url.insteadOf without touching the network); git -C <repo> remote get-url --push <remote> (applies pushInsteadOf). <remote> = team.json transport.remote, else upstream of HEAD, else 'origin'. Fork workflows are a documented risk (see risks).

PUBLISH ALGORITHM (publishOnce; mode append|compact):
  1. fetch -q --depth=1 <url> +<ref>:refs/sb/remote        -> tip, or 'no-ref' (couldn't find remote ref) => tip=null
  2. GIT_INDEX_FILE=sb-index: read-tree <tip>  | read-tree --empty
  3. rm -q -r --cached --ignore-unmatch -- state/<handle>/<machine>      (drop my whole subtree so local deletions propagate)
  4. for each local file: blob = hash-object -w --stdin (content on stdin); update-index --add --cacheinfo 100644,<blob>,state/<handle>/<machine>/<name>
  5. tree = write-tree; if tip && tree == rev-parse <tip>^{tree} => noop (nothing pushed)
  6. commit = commit-tree <tree> [-p <tip>] -m 'sb <handle>@<machine> seq=<n>'   (append: -p tip; compact: no parent)
  7. append:  push -q <pushurl> <commit>:<ref>
     compact: push -q --force-with-lease=<ref>:<tip or empty> <pushurl> <commit>:<ref>
  8. classify stderr: rejected (stale info | non-fast-forward | fetch first | failed to lock) -> retry from 1 after 300-1500 ms jitter, up to 8 attempts, then give up until the next tick (nothing is lost: local truth is republished next tick); no-ref; auth; policy (protected branch | GH006 | pre-receive hook declined); network; unknown.
  Why no merge commits: the only thing a writer contributes is 'the current content of my subtree', which is fully known locally, so a rejected commit is garbage and the rebuild on the new tip is the merge. Others' subtrees are taken verbatim from the tip. History stays linear (verified: 0 merges in 55 commits).

EXPERIMENT (scratchpad/gitlab/sbgit-exp.mjs, run 2026-09-18; git 2.39.5, Node v24.16.0; bare origin.git served over file://, user clones A (full) and B (--depth 1), hidden bare repos under A/.git/synchrobuilder/state.git and B/.git/synchrobuilder/state.git for this run). Output, trimmed:
  == 1. alice creates the ref: {"status":"pushed","tip":"dd0856a..","parent":null,"attempts":1}
     origin history: dd0856a alice sb alice@m1 ; tree: state/alice/m1/{claims,presence}.json
     user clone A refs: refs/heads/main, refs/remotes/origin/HEAD, refs/remotes/origin/main (state ref absent); status: ## main...origin/main
  == 2. bob publishes from hidden repo fetched with --depth=1: pushed, parent=dd0856a; 'hidden B is shallow: true' (push from a shallow hidden repo works); origin tree now has state/alice/m1/* and state/bob/m2/presence.json
  == 3. deterministic race (bob commits on a stale tip after alice pushed): 'stale push exit 1 -> rejected | ! [rejected] e9b07ae.. -> synchrobuilder-state (fetch first)'; recovery via normal path: pushed, parent = alice's new tip; tree keeps both writers.
  == 4. real concurrency, 3 processes x 8 publishes, tiny 50-200 ms backoff (deliberately hostile): alice 8 pushed/0 rejected, bob 8/3, carol 7 pushed + 1 gave-up after 6 rejections; 'history is linear: true | commits: 27'; every handle's last values present; wall 3.6 s.
     Rerun with 5 processes x 10 publishes and production-shaped backoff (300-1500 ms, 8 attempts): 49 pushed, 1 gave-up (racer a, 8 rejections), 55 commits on ref, wall 9.0 s. This is ~6 pushes/s against one ref with zero think time; production load is ~0.1-0.3 pushes/s for an 8-person team, and a give-up costs nothing because the next tick republishes the same local truth.
  == 5. compaction: alice pushes an orphan with --force-with-lease=<ref>:<tip>: pushed; 'origin history (1 commit expected): 68a439e alice sb alice@m1'; tree still has alice, bob, carol (nobody lost). bob then pushes an orphan with a STALE lease: 'exit 1 -> rejected | ! [rejected] b8a4ba8.. -> synchrobuilder-state (stale info)'. bob's next normal append lands on top of the compacted commit.
  == 6. `git update-ref -d` on origin: next publish recreates the ref (parent:null), others reappear on their next tick.
  == 7. removing claims.json locally removed it remotely (step 3 of the algorithm); republishing identical content -> 'noop'.
  == 8. push to refs/synchrobuilder/state: pushed; after `git fetch origin` in user clone A the ref list is unchanged except for refs/remotes/origin/synchrobuilder-state (the BRANCH form is visible to users after their next fetch; the hidden namespace is not); `git ls-remote` shows both refs/heads/synchrobuilder-state and refs/synchrobuilder/state on the server.
  == 9. classification: file:///nonexistent -> network ('does not appear to be a git repository'); http://127.0.0.1:9 -> network ('Failed to connect ... after 0 ms').
  == 10. cost: avg 121 ms per full publish cycle against the local origin (fetch + 8-10 git spawns + push); over a real network expect 0.5-3 s dominated by the two connections.
  == 11. at the end both user clones: '## main...origin/main', only branch 'main'; hidden repo config: core.bare=true and nothing else (no remotes, no worktree).
  Hidden-repo growth: after 13 depth-1 fetches carol's hidden repo had 116 loose objects and 13 lines in `shallow`; `git gc -q --prune=now` (with gc.auto=0) reduced it to 14 packed objects, 44 KB. The worker runs that gc weekly.
  Also confirmed on this run: `git rm --cached` and `update-index --cacheinfo` work in a bare repo with GIT_INDEX_FILE (no worktree needed); `commit-tree` with no -p creates the orphan; `--force-with-lease=<ref>:` (empty expected) creates a ref only if absent.

WHY THIS AND NOT THE ALTERNATIVES: (a) a normal hidden clone with a worktree would double disk use and need checkout/stash logic; index plumbing is ~10 git calls and never touches files. (b) using the user's own .git with a custom ref namespace would pollute the user's object store and, for a branch, show up in their `git branch -a` immediately; a separate bare dir keeps the user's repo byte-identical (verified). (c) two-parent merge commits (commit-tree -p tip -p mine) are unnecessary because the merge result is fully determined by 'tip tree + my subtree'; they would only add history. (d) Relay rejected git as '20-60 s behind' (prior-art-relay-notes.md L24-L25); the brief accepts that latency, and the staleness ladder from prior-art-relay-notes.md L60 (stale snapshot => context only, never ask) is adopted so the transport's lag can never block an edit.
git_commands: # one-time, hidden bare repo (H = ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/repos/<remoteKey>/state.git)
git init -q --bare --template= <H>
git --git-dir=<H> config gc.auto 0
git --git-dir=<H> config commit.gpgsign false
# read-only discovery in the USER's repo, once per session start (never in per-prompt hooks)
git -C <cwd> rev-parse --git-common-dir
git -C <repo> ls-remote --get-url <remote>          # fetch URL with url.insteadOf applied, no network
git -C <repo> remote get-url --push <remote>          # push URL with pushInsteadOf applied
# every tick (all with --git-dir=<H> -c commit.gpgsign=false -c gc.auto=0 -c core.hooksPath=<H>/nohooks; GIT_INDEX_FILE=<H>/sb-index only on the four index commands)
git fetch -q --depth=1 <fetchurl> +<ref>:refs/sb/remote     # exit 128 'couldn't find remote ref' => ref absent
git rev-parse refs/sb/remote                                   # tip
git read-tree <tip>            | git read-tree --empty          # temp index from the tip's tree
git rm -q -r --cached --ignore-unmatch -- state/<handle>/<machine>
git hash-object -w --stdin      < file content on stdin, one per file
git update-index --add --cacheinfo 100644,<blob>,state/<handle>/<machine>/<name>
git write-tree
git rev-parse <tip>^{tree}                                     # equal to write-tree output => noop, skip push
git commit-tree <tree> -p <tip> -m 'sb <handle>@<machine> seq=<n>'      # append mode (no -p when ref absent)
git commit-tree <tree> -m 'sb <handle>@<machine> seq=0 compact'         # compact mode: orphan
git push -q <pushurl> <commit>:<ref>                                        # append: server rejects non-fast-forward => rebuild
git push -q --force-with-lease=<ref>:<tip> <pushurl> <commit>:<ref>       # compact: server-side CAS, 'stale info' on mismatch
# reading others' state for the snapshot (no checkout)
git ls-tree -r -z refs/sb/remote -- state/
git cat-file --batch            < '<blob-sha>' lines on stdin (one process for all blobs)
git log -1 --format=%B refs/sb/remote                          # seq trailer for compaction trigger
# housekeeping, weekly
git gc -q --prune=now
# diagnostics (/synchrobuilder:doctor), 10 s timeout, output shown locally only
git ls-remote <fetchurl> <ref>
proposals.sync_loop:
WORKER PROCESS (worker.mjs): spawned by the SessionStart hook with spawn(process.execPath, [worker.mjs, remoteKey], {detached:true, stdio:'ignore', windowsHide:true}).unref() (experiments.md L167-L180 verified the child outlives the hook on macOS; the docs sanction 'a fully detached process' for work that must outlive a session: hooks-async-prompt-security.md L93-L97, and there is no persistent hook type: L281, L294). SessionStart itself must return within its budget: it only writes link.json + sessions/<sid>.json, kicks, spawns the worker if the lock is free, and prints the digest from the EXISTING snapshot (SessionStart runs in the background at launch and Claude's first response waits for it: hooks-events-session-and-pretool.md L59-L67; runs again on resume/compact/clear/fork: L47-L57). The worker is the baseline (conflicts.md L86-L104); a plugin monitor is only an optional accelerator because monitors are experimental, interactive-CLI-only, shell-launched and skipped where the Monitor tool is unavailable (plugins-reference.md L289-L325; monitors-tools-env.md L134-L142).
SINGLE FLIGHT: one worker per hidden repo: mkdirSync(worker.lock) atomic; lock holds {pid, startedAt}; heartbeat = touch every 10 s; another worker treats a lock older than 120 s or with a dead pid (process.kill(pid,0) throws) as stale and takes it.
TICK SCHEDULE: interval = 45 s +/- 15 s jitter (30-60 s per brief). Kick file poll every 1 s (fs.statSync mtime; no fs.watch, which is unreliable across platforms). Kicks are written by hooks on important events: claim/release, /notify send, handoff staged (Stop), session start/end, task change, contract-file edit => immediate tick, coalesced to at most one push per 2 s.
TICK BODY: (1) fetch --depth=1 => tip; on 'no-ref' tip=null. (2) read others' subtrees via ls-tree -z + one cat-file --batch process; schema-validate each JSON (size caps, types, path traversal) and drop invalid entries; write snapshot.json atomically with {v, remoteKey, tip, fetchedAt, transport:{mode, status, lastOkAt, lastError, backoffUntil}, members, claims, messagesForMe, tasks, handoffs, contracts}. (3) compose my subtree from sessions/*.json + outbox/ (all local sessions of this machine and handle); presence is rewritten every tick but is only a REASON to push if lastSeen advanced by >= presenceInterval (default 120 s), so an idle team does not commit every tick. (4) if my subtree changed or a heartbeat is due: publishOnce(append). (5) rejected => retry with 300-1500 ms jitter, 8 attempts, then wait for the next tick. (6) after a push, re-fetch is skipped (we know the tip) unless a kick arrives.
BACKOFF: network errors: 30 s, 60, 120, 240, capped 10 min, reset on success. auth: 15 min cap, status 'auth' in snapshot, doctor hint. policy (force blocked): compaction disabled for 7 days, append continues. Hidden ref namespace rejected by host: fall back to the branch ref for the rest of the day and record it.
COMPACTION: commit message trailer seq=<n> (n = tip's seq + 1). When tip seq > 2000 (or once a day at the first tick after 03:00 local, whichever first) the worker publishes in compact mode: orphan commit + --force-with-lease=<ref>:<tip>. A stale lease loses (verified 'stale info'), so a concurrent append is never overwritten. If the host answers 'policy', append-only mode continues (a year of 8 developers pushing every minute is roughly 1-2 k commits/day of ~600 packed bytes, i.e. a few hundred MB/year worst case, so compaction matters but its absence is not fatal).
EXIT: worker exits when no sessions/<sid>.json has a live CLAUDE_PID for 5 min, when it loses the lock, after 12 h (next hook respawns it), or when snapshot dir disappears. SessionEnd (1.5 s budget that plugin timeouts cannot raise: hooks-events-posttool-to-sessionend.md L349, L375) only writes a 'closed' marker and a kick; the worker pushes the final presence/handoff. Handoff content is pre-staged at every Stop (which carries last_assistant_message: hooks-events-posttool-to-sessionend.md L172; conflicts.md L106-L116).
GIT CALL TIMEOUTS: fetch 20 s, push 30 s, others 10 s, enforced by spawnSync timeout (SIGTERM); a timed-out call counts as network failure.
HOUSEKEEPING: weekly `gc -q --prune=now`; prune my messages older than 7 days or acked by all recipients; keep last 10 handoffs; cap my subtree at 64 KB.
proposals.delivery_to_claude: Hooks never run git and never touch the network; each one reads link.json (per checkout, found by walking up from the hook's cwd) and snapshot.json, both plain JSON, in a fresh `node` process (exec-form hooks: hooks-core.md L89-L105, L116; measured ~20 ms end to end for a Node hook that reads stdin and one small file: experiments.md L151-L165, leaving ~30 ms of the 50 ms budget). Delivery surfaces: (1) SessionStart (matcher startup|resume|fork|compact) prints the ~6 KB digest built from the snapshot as hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext with absolute timestamps and the snapshot's fetchedAt/transport status in the header, under the 10,000-char cap (hooks-events-session-and-pretool.md L33, L90-L112, L452); (2) UserPromptSubmit returns unread messagesForMe as additionalContext inside the labeled untrusted block plus a one-line systemMessage so the human sees that something arrived (conflicts.md L118-L130; the prompt text is read but never stored or sent); output discarded on timeout, so the hook sets a 5 s timeout and fails open (L158-L162); (3) PreToolUse Edit|Write compares the normalized tool_input.file_path (absolute, backslashes on Windows: L292-L299) against snapshot claims and returns additionalContext (warn) or permissionDecision ask (opt-in), applying the staleness ladder: snapshot older than 5 min => context only, never ask (prior-art-relay-notes.md L60, L199); at most once per file per 30 min via wx marker files; (4) PostToolUse Edit|Write guard re-audits the file and records contract-file edits into the local outbox + kick (synchronous, additionalContext lands next to the tool result in the same turn: hooks-events-posttool-to-sessionend.md L67, L363); (5) Stop stages the handoff draft from last_assistant_message into the local journal; (6) SessionEnd writes the closed marker only. 'Sooner than next prompt' delivery is out of scope for the transport itself: the worker can optionally feed a plugin monitor (one stdout line per urgent message) or post to the session's own inbox socket (agent-teams-and-cross-session-messaging.md L345), both listed as experiments. Every teammate-authored string is wrapped in a labeled data block and phrased as facts, not instructions (hooks-core.md L335).
proposals.offline_and_failure_behavior:
Guiding rule: the worker fails, hooks never do. Hooks only read local JSON; if link.json or snapshot.json is missing or malformed they emit nothing and exit 0 (hooks-core.md L211-L214, L363). The snapshot always carries transport.status and fetchedAt so the digest can say 'team state as of 10:32Z, remote unreachable since 10:35Z'.
OFFLINE / NETWORK DOWN: fetch fails => classified 'network', snapshot keeps the last good merged state (never overwritten with a failure), backoff 30 s..10 min; local sessions keep writing outbox/sessions files; my subtree is regenerated from that local truth on the first successful tick, so nothing is queued or lost, and no queue can grow unbounded (the outbox is state, not events; messages expire after 7 days).
MISSING REMOTE: no remote name resolves or `ls-remote --get-url` fails => transport.status 'no-remote', worker still runs to build a local-only snapshot (my own claims still warn my other sessions), digest says the team channel is off, /synchrobuilder:doctor explains.
AUTH FAILURE (Authentication failed | Permission denied (publickey) | could not read Username | 401/403): status 'auth', 15-min backoff, no prompts ever (GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GCM_INTERACTIVE=never, SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never; hooks have no controlling terminal anyway: hooks-core.md L345). READ-ONLY COLLABORATOR (fetch ok, push 403): status 'read-only', keep consuming others' state, digest notes that the user's presence is invisible to teammates.
FORCE PUSH BY ANYONE: fetch uses a '+' refspec so refs/sb/remote is force-updated; every build starts from the current tip and regenerates my subtree, so a force push that dropped my files is repaired on my next tick and one that dropped others' is repaired on theirs (verified in scenario 5 where an orphan compaction replaced the whole history and appends continued on top).
REF DELETED: 'no-ref' => next publish recreates it with no parent (verified scenario 6).
HOST BLOCKS FORCE/NON-FF: classified 'policy' => compaction disabled 7 days, append continues; doctor reports it.
SHALLOW USER CLONE: irrelevant; the hidden repo is separate (verified with a --depth 1 user clone). Shallow HIDDEN repo (fetch --depth=1 every tick) pushes fine (verified) and stays small with weekly gc (116 loose objects -> 44 KB).
TWO WORKERS: mkdir lock + pid liveness; a second one exits immediately; a stale lock is taken over after 120 s.
GIT MISSING FROM PATH: worker cannot start; SessionStart logs it locally, doctor reports 'git not found'; hooks continue with whatever snapshot exists. NODE MISSING: exec-form hooks cannot start at all and Claude Code shows a hook error notice on every event but never blocks (experiments.md L126-L149); doctor is the only remedy.
WORKER CRASH: uncaughtException/unhandledRejection handlers log locally and exit 0; the next hook respawns. SESSION KILLED WITHOUT SessionEnd (undocumented whether it fires on terminal close: hooks-events-posttool-to-sessionend.md L350, L382): the worker notices the dead CLAUDE_PID within one tick and publishes 'offline' presence; the staged handoff journal is published at the next session start.
GIVE-UP AFTER 8 REJECTIONS: nothing lost; next tick republishes local truth (the publish is idempotent).
host_compatibility: Plain git (bare repo over file://, ssh, or http smart protocol): fully verified locally on git 2.39.5 for both refs/heads/synchrobuilder-state and refs/synchrobuilder/state, including non-fast-forward rejection, --force-with-lease CAS ('stale info'), push from a depth-1 shallow repo, ref deletion/recreation. Assumption: the same holds for git >= 2.20 on the client; --force-with-lease with an explicit expected sha has existed since git 1.8.5.

GitHub: branch form should work anywhere pushes are allowed; UNVERIFIED and must be tested: (a) whether pushes to refs/synchrobuilder/* (custom namespace) are accepted, (b) whether rulesets/branch protection that 'block force pushes' apply repo-wide to a non-protected branch name (then compaction is disabled automatically via the 'policy' class), (c) whether an 'author email must be verified/match' ruleset rejects <handle>@synchrobuilder.invalid, (d) GH006 message text for classification, (e) whether GitHub's web UI or default fetch ever surfaces refs/synchrobuilder/*. Also: `owner/repo` shorthand cloning via SSH vs HTTPS is a marketplace-install concern, not this transport's (conflicts.md L162-L177).

GitLab: UNVERIFIED: custom ref namespaces, push rules 'reject unverified users' / 'check author is a GitLab user' (would reject the noreply author; fallback to git config user.email is designed in), 'prevent force push' scope, and whether the state branch counts toward any per-project branch limits.
Bitbucket Cloud / Server (Data Center): UNVERIFIED: custom ref acceptance, force-push restrictions, and whether 'branch permissions' patterns like * catch the state branch.
Azure DevOps: UNVERIFIED: custom refs are historically restricted; expect to need the branch form; verify force-push policy text for classification.
Gitea/Forgejo/Gogs/self-hosted bare repos: expected to behave like plain git; UNVERIFIED with their protected-branch features.

Any host with server-side pre-receive hooks (commit message lint, signed-commit enforcement, author allow-lists): our commits are unsigned with a fixed message template; failures classify as 'policy' and the doctor shows the server's message verbatim. Signed commits are explicitly disabled (-c commit.gpgsign=false) so a background worker can never hang on a passphrase.
Public repositories: everything on the state ref is readable by the world; the digest/doctor must say so and teams should treat message text accordingly (security_notes).
proposals.windows_notes:
Verified facts from the docs: exec-form `node` + args runs with no shell on every platform and .cmd/.bat shims must never be named (windows-notes.md L54-L74; hooks-core.md L95); CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/DATA/PROJECT_DIR are exported to hook processes in both forms (windows-notes.md L80-L83); `~/.claude` is %USERPROFILE%\.claude, so the hidden repo lives under %USERPROFILE%\.claude\plugins\data\<id>\repos\... unless CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR moves it (windows-notes.md L241); tool_input.file_path arrives with backslashes and drive letter, so claim paths are stored repo-relative with forward slashes and compared after normalization, never anchored with ^ (windows-notes.md L119-L142); git must be on PATH for a git-hosted marketplace anyway (windows-notes.md L240), so requiring git for the transport adds no new prerequisite; link-mode plugins are refused on Windows (L243), irrelevant here because the hidden repo is not part of the plugin.
Design decisions for Windows (assumptions marked): spawnSync('git', argv) resolves git.exe through libuv's PATH search without a shell (assumption from Node/libuv behavior, needs the CI run); the worker is spawned with process.execPath (absolute node.exe) and {detached:true, stdio:'ignore', windowsHide:true} + unref() so it survives the hook and shows no console window (documented Node semantics; the docs' detach sanction is platform-neutral: hooks-async-prompt-security.md L93-L107; only macOS was measured: experiments.md L167-L180); every path handed to git is absolute and native, every path INSIDE the tree is generated by us with forward slashes; blobs are written via hash-object --stdin with no --path, so core.autocrlf never rewrites them (assumption to verify); gc.auto=0 avoids git spawning a background `gc --auto` that can fail on locked files; snapshot.json is replaced with renameSync and retried 5x20 ms on EPERM/EBUSY because a reader may hold the file open; the worker lock uses mkdirSync (atomic on NTFS); Git Credential Manager is kept from opening a GUI with GCM_INTERACTIVE=never and Windows OpenSSH from prompting with SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never (harmless if unsupported); no reliance on chmod, shebangs or Git Bash (windows-notes.md L305). Two Windows configurations must be in CI (Git Bash present and absent: windows-notes.md L296) although the transport itself never uses either shell. Open Windows questions that only a runner can answer: drive-letter casing in file_path (L335), backslash vs slash in the substituted ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} (L336), node startup time under Defender (L338), and whether `git rm --cached` + GIT_INDEX_FILE behave identically in a bare repo on NTFS (expected yes).
proposals.security_notes:
TRUST MODEL: anyone with push access to the team remote can write anything on the state ref, including files under another handle's subtree; git itself does not authenticate writers per path. So the transport gives integrity against ACCIDENTS (one writer per file, CAS pushes) but not against a malicious collaborator; impersonation resistance is deferred to the hosted-hub tier or to optional per-member ed25519 signatures over each JSON file (public keys in team.json), which the Transport interface leaves room for. Doctor and docs must say this plainly (no fake evidence).
UNTRUSTED INPUT: every blob read from the ref is untrusted data. The snapshot builder validates schema version, types, string lengths (message text 500, handoff 4 KB, subtree 64 KB), rejects any `path` containing `..`, a drive letter, a leading `/`, or a NUL, ignores unknown handles not in team.json (kept in a separate 'unknown' bucket), never follows symlinks (we never check out; ls-tree/cat-file only, and mode 120000 or 160000 entries are skipped), never executes or imports anything from the ref (hooks-async-prompt-security.md L136-L146). Teammate strings reach Claude only inside a labeled data block phrased as facts (hooks-core.md L335).
PRIVACY (what leaves the machine): handle, machine hash (sha256 of hostname+user+salt, 8 hex), repo-relative file paths, branch name, timestamps, claim/task/message/handoff text the user or the plugin authored, contract-alert paths + commit shas. Never: prompts, transcripts, source contents or diffs, environment values, absolute paths, hostnames, emails (commit author is <handle>@synchrobuilder.invalid by default; the git-config email fallback is opt-in per team and only used when a host rejects the noreply author). A regex secret-redaction pass (own implementation, MIT-licensed reuse of Relay's pattern list must carry its notice: prior-art-relay-notes.md L129) runs over every free-text field before it is written to the outbox. The UserPromptSubmit hook receives the prompt but stores nothing from it. The state ref is exactly as visible as the repository; public repos publish the team's presence to the world, which the setup command must state before enabling.
GIT PROCESS HYGIENE: argv arrays only (no shell), env allow/deny list that strips GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE etc. so the user's repo can never be addressed by accident, --git-dir always explicit, cwd = hidden dir, --template= at init and core.hooksPath pointed at an empty dir so global templates/hooks cannot inject code, commit.gpgsign=false, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and the askpass suppressors so a background worker can never hang or pop a GUI. The user's repo-local config is NOT inherited; if a CI-style `http.<url>.extraheader` or `credential.helper` lives only there, pushes fail with 'auth' and doctor says why. A future option is to forward selected repo-local `credential.*`/`http.*` keys via GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n/VALUE_n environment (git >= 2.31) rather than argv, so tokens never appear in process listings; listed as an experiment.
CONSENT: creating the hidden repo and pushing the first commit happens only after /synchrobuilder:setup shows the ref name, remote URL and the exact list of fields that will be published; the SessionStart hook never creates the ref on its own (brief: consent before changing a machine; hooks run automatically once enabled: hooks-core.md L382).
LOCAL FILES: everything under ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} is per user; logs contain git stderr (which can include the remote URL, never credentials since git redacts them) and are capped at 1 MB with rotation.
proposals.complexity_estimate: Roughly 900-1,200 lines of dependency-free Node ESM across: git runner + error classifier (~120), Transport interface + git implementation (~300, of which the publish loop is ~80 and was prototyped in the experiment script), snapshot builder/validator (~200), worker (lock, tick scheduler, kicks, backoff, compaction, gc, exit rules; ~250), per-checkout link/discovery at SessionStart (~80), hook read path helper (~60), doctor checks (~100). Tests: the experiment harness (bare origin + N hidden repos + parallel racers) becomes the integration suite and runs in about 15 s; add fixture-based unit tests for the classifier, validator and snapshot merge. Effort: 2-3 engineer-weeks for macOS/Linux including tests, plus 1 week for Windows CI and the host matrix experiments. Runtime cost: ~121 ms CPU per publish locally, one network round trip per tick per machine, hooks unchanged at ~20 ms.
risks: Host policy: repo-wide 'block force pushes' or custom-ref rejection would silently disable compaction or the hidden namespace; handled by classification + fallback, but the append-only history can reach a few hundred MB/year for busy teams. Mitigation: presence heartbeat interval 120 s, push only on change, doctor visibility, and a documented manual reset (delete the branch) as last resort.
Impersonation: any collaborator with push access can write another handle's subtree; git gives no per-path authentication. Documented limitation; signatures or the hub tier are the fix.

Fork workflows: if a developer's 'origin' is their fork, their state goes to the fork and never meets the team's. Mitigation: team.json transport.remote and a doctor check that compares the remote URL to the URL hash pinned in team.json.

Detached worker lifetime on Windows and Linux is measured only on macOS (experiments.md L167-L180); if a platform reaps it with the hook, the fallback is a bounded sync inside an async PostToolUse/UserPromptSubmit hook, which -p sessions kill at teardown (hooks-async-prompt-security.md L42-L49).

Credential edge cases: repo-local-only credential config, SSH keys with passphrases and no agent, GCM GUI prompts on Windows, 2FA-expired tokens: all classify as 'auth' and stall silently for 15 min at a time; the only remedy is doctor. Nothing in the transport can or should prompt.

Presence granularity is 30-60 s plus network; collision warnings must be worded 'edited by X within the last N minutes as of HH:MMZ' (prior-art-relay-notes.md L199), never 'editing now'; a stale snapshot must never produce an ask.

Visibility: the branch form appears as origin/synchrobuilder-state in every teammate's `git branch -r` after their next fetch (verified) and in the host's branch list; some teams will object. The hidden namespace avoids it but is host-dependent (experiment).

CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB may strip CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA from hook processes (not stated: monitors-tools-env.md L368); the git-common-dir fallback location covers it but changes where the hidden repo lives on those machines.

Server-side commit rules (verified-email rulesets, signed-commit enforcement, message lint) reject our noreply author or unsigned commits; classification shows the server text, and the git-config-email fallback covers the common case, but signed-commit enforcement cannot be met by a background worker.
Public repositories publish presence and messages to the world; the setup consent screen must make this explicit.
git or node not on the PATH of the hook process (Desktop-launched sessions with a minimal PATH: prior-art-relay-notes.md L231) disables the worker or every hook; only doctor can help.

Clock skew between machines affects staleness math; all timestamps are producer-side UTC and the snapshot records fetchedAt on the consumer, so the ladder uses same-clock age arithmetic where possible.

proposals.name: Per-writer refs: refs/synchrobuilder/v1/<handle>/<device> orphan snapshots, published from a plugin-owned shadow bare repo
proposals.summary: Each (developer, device) pair owns exactly one ref on the team's existing remote, `refs/synchrobuilder/v1/<handle>/<device>`, whose tip is always a single parentless commit holding only that writer's state files. Writers rebuild that commit from local journal files with git plumbing (hash-object, mktree, commit-tree, update-ref) and `push --force-with-lease`; readers fetch `+refs/synchrobuilder/v1/*:refs/synchrobuilder-remote/v1/*`, read every writer's tree with `cat-file --batch`, and fold the union into `snapshot.json` under `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}`. Nothing is ever merged: ownership is the ref name, so concurrent pushes cannot conflict, a bad writer's blast radius is its own ref, and a stale developer is garbage-collected by deleting one ref. All git work happens in a plugin-owned bare "shadow" repo under `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}`, never in the user's `.git`, so shallow clones, worktrees, IDE lock contention and `git log --all` noise are all avoided; hooks only read the local snapshot. Verified locally with git 2.39.5 in a throwaway bare hub plus two clones, a shallow clone and a shadow repo (commands and output in `mechanism`). Host acceptance of custom ref namespaces is the one thing I could not verify from this Mac; the design carries a probe-and-fallback ladder (custom namespace, then `refs/heads/synchrobuilder/...` branches, then read-only) and the host questions are listed under experiments_needed rather than asserted.
proposals.mechanism:
## 1. Naming and ownership

- Ref per writer: `refs/synchrobuilder/v1/<handle>/<device>`. `<handle>` comes from the identity ladder (`git config user.email` mapped through `.synchrobuilder/team.json`, `/synchrobuilder:iam` override, per-machine placeholder otherwise; prior-art-relay-notes.md L206). `<device>` is a random 8-char id generated once and stored in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/device.json` (not the hostname; privacy). Both segments are forced to `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$` before use. Reason for per-device rather than per-handle refs: one developer with a laptop and a desktop would otherwise force-push over themselves; with per-device refs "one writer per ref" is literally true and no lease juggling is needed. Lowercase is mandatory because the shadow repo stores loose refs as files and macOS/Windows filesystems are case-insensitive (`Alice`/`alice` would collide).
- `git check-ref-format` accepts this shape and rejects spaces, `..` and `.lock` suffixes (verified, see experiment output below); `v1` is a schema version so a future incompatible layout can live beside the old one.
- Tree layout inside a writer's commit (flat, small JSON, all written by this writer only):
  - `manifest.json` `{schema:1, handle, device, generated_at, files:[...]}` (reader rejects a ref whose manifest handle/device do not match the ref name)
  - `presence.json` (sessions on this device: session id hash, cwd repo-relative area, branch name, last_seen, objective <=140 chars)
  - `claims.json` (repo-relative paths, reason <=200 chars, expires_at)
  - `messages/<ulid>.json` (from `/synchrobuilder:notify`: to handle or `*`, text <=2 KB after secret redaction, expires_at)
  - `tasks/<taskId>.json` for tasks this writer created, `task-events/<ulid>.json` for state changes this writer made to anyone's task (reader folds by timestamp, handle as tiebreak)
  - `handoffs/<sessionIdHash>.json`, `contracts/<ulid>.json` (paths + short content hash, never hunks)
  - Caps enforced by both writer and reader: <=64 KB per file, <=500 files, <=1 MB per writer.
- The commit is always parentless ("orphan snapshot"). Verified: `git rev-list --count` on a fetched writer ref is `1` and the commit has `0` parent lines. Unchanged blobs are shared across snapshots by content hash, so a push transfers only the changed blobs plus one tree and one commit.

## 2. Shadow repo instead of the user's `.git`

All git runs in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/remotes/<remoteKey>/git/` (a bare repo; `remoteKey = sha256(normalizedRemoteUrl).slice(0,12)`), created with `git init --bare` and `git remote add origin <url>`. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` is the documented persistent directory that survives plugin updates (plugins-reference.md L163, L182) and is exported to hook processes (plugins-reference.md L166; experiments.md L107-L110), whereas `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` changes on every update (plugins-reference.md L174). Consequences:
- The user's working tree, index, branches, `packed-refs`, `git log --all` and `git push --mirror` are never touched by us (the brief's "never touch the user's working tree or normal branches").
- Shallow clones and linked worktrees are irrelevant: the shadow repo is our own full (tiny) repo. (Fetching our refs into a `--depth 1` clone also works, verified below, but we do not need it.)
- Auth reuses the developer's global git configuration (credential helpers, SSH keys, `url.*.insteadOf`). Repo-local settings the user may have (`http.*`, `credential.*`, `core.sshCommand`, `url.*`) are copied into the shadow config at init via `git config --local --get-regexp` and refreshed when the user's config mtime changes. Alternative verified locally: `git -C shadow.git -c include.path=<user>/.git/config config --get http.extraHeader` returned the user's value, so the whole local config can be layered per invocation instead; I recommend copying selected keys because `include.path` would also import the user's `remote.origin.fetch` refspec.
- The remote URL comes from the user's repo (`git -C <cwd> remote get-url <name>` once, at SessionStart, which runs in the background and whose only cost is that Claude's first response waits for it: hooks-events-session-and-pretool.md L61). `<name>` is `origin` unless `.synchrobuilder/config.json` sets `remote` (forks: teams that push to personal forks must point this at the shared repo).

## 3. Writer path (one sync tick with changes)

Five spawns, all `child_process.execFile('git', [...argv])`, no shell, cwd-independent (`git -C <shadow>`), measured 53.7 ms end to end on this Mac before the push:

1. `git hash-object -w --no-filters --stdin` per file (or `--stdin-paths` over a staging dir to make it one spawn)
2. `git mktree` with `100644 blob <sha>\t<path>` lines on stdin
3. `git commit-tree <tree> -m "synchrobuilder <handle>/<device> <iso-time>"` (no `-p`; author/committer = the developer's real git identity so host push rules that check author email still pass)
4. `git update-ref refs/synchrobuilder/v1/<h>/<d> <commit>`
5. `git push --quiet --force-with-lease=refs/synchrobuilder/v1/<h>/<d>:<lastKnownRemoteSha> origin refs/synchrobuilder/v1/<h>/<d>:refs/synchrobuilder/v1/<h>/<d>` (first push uses an empty expected value, meaning "must not exist")

A tick with no content change and a fresh heartbeat (< heartbeat interval) skips all five.

## 4. Reader path (one sync tick)

1. `git ls-remote --quiet origin 'refs/synchrobuilder/v1/*'` (one round trip; under protocol v2 the client sends `ref-prefix refs/synchrobuilder/v1/`, verified with `GIT_TRACE_PACKET=1`, so the server lists only our refs, not every branch). Compare with the previous listing; if nothing changed, stop.
2. Sanity rule learned from experiment E-N2: if the listing lacks our own ref although we pushed successfully in the last 10 minutes, the host is hiding or has purged the namespace; mark the snapshot `transport: "degraded"` and do NOT prune (a prune against a hidden namespace deleted every local mirror ref in the experiment).
3. `git fetch --quiet --prune origin '+refs/synchrobuilder/v1/*:refs/synchrobuilder-remote/v1/*'` (the leading `+` accepts the non-fast-forward updates that every force-push produces; `--prune` with an explicit refspec removes mirrors of deleted writer refs, verified).
4. `git for-each-ref --format='%(refname) %(objectname) %(tree) %(committerdate:unix)' refs/synchrobuilder-remote/v1/`
5. `git cat-file --batch` fed the tree ids (parse the binary tree format in Node), then `git cat-file --batch` fed all blob ids: three spawns regardless of team size.
6. Validate every writer (schema, caps, manifest matches ref name, timestamps clamped to now+5 min), fold into `snapshot.json` (tmp file + rename), plus `statusline.txt` and `inbox/<handle>/…` for delivered messages. Writers are keyed by ref name; a handle's presence is the union over its devices.

Measured on this Mac with 2 writers, 4 blobs, local file remote: push 30 ms, fetch --prune 26 ms, read all trees and blobs 30 ms.

## 5. Namespace probe and fallback ladder

At `/synchrobuilder:setup` (with consent) and again on the first tick after any namespace rejection, the worker pushes its own ref and interprets the result:
- Success: `mode = "refs"` (hidden from host UIs, exempt from branch rules; see host_compatibility).
- `! [remote rejected]` / `pre-receive hook declined` / host-specific messages: try `refs/heads/synchrobuilder/v1/<h>/<d>` (a visible branch; same plumbing, same reader refspec added as `+refs/heads/synchrobuilder/v1/*:refs/synchrobuilder-remote/v1/*`).
- `(non-fast-forward)` rejection in branch mode (a "block force pushes on all branches" policy, or `receive.denyNonFastForwards=true` on a self-hosted bare repo, verified locally): switch that writer to a parented fast-forward chain (`commit-tree -p <previous>`) and attempt a re-root (orphan + force) once a day; if re-root is refused the chain simply grows (about 1 KB/commit) and `/synchrobuilder:doctor` reports it.
- Still rejected, or no push permission (read-only collaborators): `mode = "read-only"`; the developer still receives everyone else's state, and doctor explains why they are invisible.
Readers always fetch both namespaces, so mixed-mode teams work. The mode is recorded in the shadow config and in `manifest.json`.

## 6. Garbage collection of stale developers and devices

- Ref-level: any writer's worker, at most once per hour and only when its own push succeeded, runs the janitor: for every remote ref whose tip `committerdate` is older than `staleRefDays` (default 30, configurable in `.synchrobuilder/config.json`), `git push --quiet origin --delete <ref>`. Deleting an already-deleted ref only warns (`remote: warning: deleting a non-existent ref`, exit 0, verified), so two janitors racing is harmless. A returning developer or a re-imaged device simply re-creates its ref at the next tick (lease "must not exist" fails, then a plain `--force` succeeds).
- `/synchrobuilder:leave` deletes the caller's own refs immediately; uninstalling the plugin deletes `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` (plugins-reference.md L186) but not the remote ref, which the janitor removes after `staleRefDays`.
- Object-level on the host: each force-push makes the previous snapshot unreachable; hosts reclaim unreachable objects with their own gc. Verified on the bare hub: after 20 ticks `count: 101` loose objects, `git gc --prune=now` left `count: 0, in-pack: 12`. Growth is ~4 KB per tick per writer before gc.
- Local: `git fetch --prune` keeps the mirror refs exact; weekly `git gc --quiet --prune=1.day` in the shadow repo (`gc.autoDetach=false` so no background gc daemons are left behind).

## 7. Local experiment record (git 2.39.5, macOS, scratchpad `refs-experiment/`, script `run.sh` + `time.mjs`)

Setup: `git init --bare hub.git`; clones `alice`, `bob`; `git clone --depth 1 file://…/hub.git carol` (`rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` → `true`); `git init --bare shadow.git` + `remote add origin`.

- E-B (alice, plumbing only): `hash-object -w --stdin` x2, `mktree`, `commit-tree`, `update-ref refs/synchrobuilder/v1/alice/mac1`, then `git push --force origin refs/synchrobuilder/v1/alice/mac1:refs/synchrobuilder/v1/alice/mac1` → ` * [new reference]   refs/synchrobuilder/v1/alice/mac1 -> refs/synchrobuilder/v1/alice/mac1`; `git status --porcelain | wc -l` → `0` (working tree untouched).
- E-C: `git ls-remote origin 'refs/synchrobuilder/*'` lists the ref; `git -C hub.git branch --list` shows only `* main`.
- E-D (bob): `git fetch origin` (default refspec) → `0` mirror refs; `git fetch origin '+refs/synchrobuilder/v1/*:refs/synchrobuilder-remote/v1/*'` → ` * [new ref] … -> refs/synchrobuilder-remote/v1/alice/mac1`.
- E-E: `git ls-tree -r`, `git cat-file -p <ref>:claims.json` and `git cat-file --batch` return the JSON without any checkout.
- E-F: `git branch -a` does not show the ref; `git log --all --oneline` does show the orphan commit (the reason the shadow repo, not the user's `.git`, holds these refs).
- E-G: second orphan pushed with `--force-with-lease=<ref>:<sha1>` → ` + 272f1cd...b2d596e … (forced update)`; bob's `+` refspec fetch → ` + 272f1cd...b2d596e … (forced update)` and the new manifest reads `"seq":2`.
- E-H2 (stale lease): after another writer moved the remote ref, `push --force-with-lease=<ref>:<oldsha>` → ` ! [rejected] … (stale info)`; with the current sha → ` + … (forced update)`.
- E-I: `git -C hub.git config receive.denyNonFastForwards true` → orphan force push ` ! [rejected] … (non-fast-forward)` exit 1; a commit with `-p <previous>` pushes cleanly. (Basis for the fast-forward fallback.)
- E-J (shallow clone carol): custom-ref fetch and `cat-file` work, exit 0.
- E-K (shadow bare repo): fetch of the namespace and a push of `refs/synchrobuilder/v1/bob/pc1` both succeed; `count-objects` → 6 loose objects.
- E-L: glob refspec with zero matches → exit 0 silently; literal missing ref → `fatal: couldn't find remote ref …` exit 128 (so the reader must use the glob form).
- E-M: `git push origin --delete refs/synchrobuilder/v1/alice/mac1` → ` - [deleted]`; repeating it → `remote: warning: deleting a non-existent ref`, exit 0; bob's `fetch --prune` with the explicit refspec → ` - [deleted] (none) -> refs/synchrobuilder-remote/v1/alice/mac1`.
- E-N2: `uploadpack.hideRefs refs/synchrobuilder` on the hub → `ls-remote` lists 0 refs and `fetch --prune` deleted both local mirror refs with exit 0 (hence rule 4.2 above).
- E-O: `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git ls-remote nosuchremote` → `fatal: 'nosuchremote' does not appear to be a git repository`, exit 128; `https://127.0.0.1:9/...` → `Couldn't connect to server`, exit 128, immediately.
- E-P: `git -C alice push --mirror origin` from a clone that never fetched our refs → ` - [deleted] refs/synchrobuilder/v1/bob/pc1` (mirror pushes wipe our refs; each writer's next tick re-creates its own ref, so this self-heals within one interval, but it is listed under risks).
- Timing (`time.mjs`, shadow repo, local file remote): `build tree+commit (5 spawns): 53.7 ms; push --force: 30.0 ms; fetch --prune: 26.2 ms; read all trees+blobs (4 spawns): 30.4 ms`.
- Protocol v2 trace of `fetch` with the refspec: `fetch> ref-prefix refs/synchrobuilder/v1/` (plus `refs/tags/` from the default tag-following, disable with `--no-tags`).
- `git check-ref-format`: `…/alice/mac1` ok; `…/al ice/x`, `…/x.lock`, `…/a..b/x` rejected; `…/-alice/x` accepted by git but forbidden by our regex anyway.

## 8. Transport interface (so a hub can replace git later)

`interface Transport { probe(): Promise<Mode>; publish(files: Map<string, Uint8Array>, meta): Promise<{tip: string}>; list(): Promise<WriterRef[]>; pull(changed: WriterRef[]): Promise<WriterTree[]>; retire(writerId): Promise<void>; health(): TransportHealth }`. `GitRefsTransport` is the only v1 implementation; the sync engine, fold logic, snapshot writer and hooks never see git. A future `HubTransport` implements the same five calls over HTTPS.

proposals.sync_loop:
**Process model.** There is no long-lived hook type; each async hook firing is a fresh process and `-p` sessions kill async hooks at teardown (hooks-async-prompt-security.md L46-L47, L281). So the loop is a detached Node worker (`spawn(process.execPath, [worker.mjs, remoteKey], {detached:true, stdio:'ignore', windowsHide:true}).unref()`), which experiment E5 showed outlives its parent hook on macOS (experiments.md L171-L178); Linux and Windows are still to be verified (experiments.md L180; hooks-async-prompt-security.md L303). This matches conflicts.md L98-L100 (worker started from SessionStart, exits when `CLAUDE_PID` disappears). Plugin monitors are only an optional accelerator because they run through a shell, only in interactive CLI sessions, and not where the Monitor tool is unavailable (plugins-reference.md L291-L293, L321; monitors-tools-env.md L118, L140).

**Registration.** The SessionStart hook (exec-form `node`, hooks-core.md L361) writes `${DATA}/remotes/<remoteKey>/sessions/<session_id>.json` with `pid = CLAUDE_PID` (monitors-tools-env.md L278; v2.1.214+), cwd, branch, handle; it also appends the repo top-level path to `${DATA}/index.json` so later hooks can find the snapshot without spawning git. Then it tries to start the worker: `fs.openSync(worker.lock, 'wx')` writing its pid; if the lock exists and `process.kill(pid, 0)` succeeds, a worker is already running (single-flight per device per remote, which is what makes "one writer per ref" true even with several Claude sessions or clones on one machine); if the pid is dead, the lock is stale and is taken over.

**Tick.** Base interval 30 s in the first 10 minutes of a session, then 45 s, jitter ±5 s (the brief's 30-60 s window). Each tick: (1) gather local state: live sessions (pid check), journal files the hooks append (`journal/<session>.jsonl`: claims, releases, edits, task events, notify outbox, handoff draft staged at every Stop per conflicts.md L112-L113), mute list excluded; (2) render this device's tree; (3) if content changed, or heartbeat older than `heartbeatSeconds` (default 120 active, 600 idle), run the writer path; (4) run the reader path and rewrite `snapshot.json`, `statusline.txt`, per-handle inbox; (5) hourly: janitor + config refresh; weekly: gc.

**Immediate push on important events.** The claim, release, notify, handoff and contract-change hooks touch `${DATA}/remotes/<key>/wake/<ulid>`; the worker watches that directory with `fs.watch` (polling fallback every 2 s on filesystems where `fs.watch` is unreliable) and runs a tick immediately, with a floor of 5 s between pushes so bursts coalesce.

**Backoff.** Per operation class, exponential with jitter: network errors (`Could not resolve host`, `Connection timed out`, `Couldn't connect`) 30 s → 1 → 2 → 4 min, cap 5 min; auth errors (`Authentication failed`, `Permission denied (publickey)`, `403`, `terminal prompts disabled`) cap 15 min and a doctor note; ref rejections (`remote rejected`, `pre-receive hook declined`, `non-fast-forward`) trigger the fallback ladder once, then read-only for 1 h; `stale info` (lease) → re-list, then one plain `--force`. Reads keep running on their own schedule even while pushes are backing off, so the developer still sees the team.

**Exit.** When no registered session pid is alive for two consecutive ticks, the worker pushes a final tree whose presence entries carry `last_seen` (readers age presence out; no "offline" flag needs to be true), releases the lock and exits. A worker whose parent Claude Code died without SessionEnd exits the same way, and the handoff drafted at the last Stop is pushed by the next session's worker (conflicts.md L112-L116; SessionEnd itself has a 1.5 s budget that plugin timeouts cannot raise, hooks-events-posttool-to-sessionend.md L349, L364).

**Logging.** `${DATA}/log/sync.log`, rotated at 1 MB, one line per tick with timings and the classified error; never any file contents.
proposals.delivery_to_claude:
Hooks never touch git or the network; they read `snapshot.json` (and small per-session marker files) from `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}`, which is exported to hook processes (plugins-reference.md L166; experiments.md L107). A Node exec-form hook that reads stdin plus one cache file costs about 20 ms end to end on this laptop (experiments.md L157, L162), which leaves room under the brief's 50 ms budget; the hook finds the snapshot by walking up from `cwd` to the `.git` entry and looking the path up in `${DATA}/index.json` (no spawn).

- **Session digest**: a `type: "command"` SessionStart hook is the documented vehicle; at launch it runs in the background and Claude's first response waits for it (hooks-events-session-and-pretool.md L61, L452). It emits `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` (~6 KB, under the 10,000-character cap, hooks-core.md L271) rendered from the snapshot: team now, claims touching my area, messages for me, handoffs since my last session, my last handoff. Every line carries an absolute UTC timestamp and the snapshot's `fetched_at`, because mid-session hook text is replayed verbatim on resume while SessionStart re-runs (hooks-core.md L337). Re-inject on `compact`; `sessionTitle` only on startup/resume/fork.
- **Notify landing in the next prompt**: the UserPromptSubmit hook returns `additionalContext` with unread inbox messages wrapped in a labeled data block, plus a one-line `systemMessage` so the human sees that something arrived (hooks-events-session-and-pretool.md L453; conflicts.md L128-L130). Messages are marked delivered by a `wx` marker file keyed by ulid (race-free once-only, prior-art-relay-notes.md L127). "Sooner" delivery is optional and layered: a plugin monitor where available, or the own-session inbox socket (`CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET`, v2.1.224+; agent-teams-and-cross-session-messaging.md L345, L347) posted by the worker, never by a hook.
- **Claims / collision warnings**: PreToolUse on `Edit|Write|NotebookEdit` normalizes backslashes in `tool_input.file_path` (hooks-events-session-and-pretool.md L299; windows-notes.md L313), compares the repo-relative path against other handles' claims and recent edits in the snapshot, and returns `additionalContext` (warn mode) or `permissionDecision: "ask"` plus `permissionDecisionReason` (ask mode, team opt-in) (hooks-events-session-and-pretool.md L454). Wording is factual and time-stamped ("claimed by bob 12 min ago as of 10:42Z"), never "editing right now", because the transport is 30-60 s behind (prior-art-relay-notes.md L199). Staleness ladder: snapshot older than 15 min, or `transport: "degraded"`, downgrades ask to context; once per file per 30 min via `wx` marker files.
- **Guard**: unchanged; synchronous PostToolUse `additionalContext` lands next to the tool result in the same turn (hooks-events-posttool-to-sessionend.md L363).
- **Task board / handoff / contract alerts**: rendered from the folded snapshot in `/synchrobuilder:team`, `:board`, and the digest; hooks only append to the local journal.
- **Status line**: a plugin cannot ship `statusLine` (statusline-and-settings.md L218, L401); `/synchrobuilder:setup` may, with consent, write a user-settings `statusLine` running `node <DATA>/statusline.mjs` that only reads `statusline.txt` pre-rendered by the worker, with `refreshInterval` 15-30 s (statusline-and-settings.md L402-L403).
- **Untrusted text**: everything read from a writer ref is data. It is schema-validated, capped, and injected only inside a labeled block that states the four limits Claude Code itself uses for peer messages (cannot approve, cannot change configuration, commands are plain text, permissions still apply; agent-teams-and-cross-session-messaging.md L346), written as statements not commands (hooks-core.md L335).
proposals.offline_and_failure_behavior:
- **Offline**: hooks keep working from the last `snapshot.json` (its `fetched_at` drives the staleness ladder, so warnings degrade to context after 15 min and never block). Local state (claims, messages, handoffs, task events) lives in the journal, and the tree is rebuilt from it on every tick, so nothing is "lost while offline": the next successful push carries everything, and message expiry (`expires_at`, default 7 days) is evaluated by readers, not by the queue. No separate outbox is needed because the writer ref is itself the outbox.
- **Missing remote / not a git repo**: SessionStart finds no remote; the worker runs in local-only mode (multi-session presence on one machine still works from the journal) and `/synchrobuilder:doctor` explains; hooks emit nothing extra. Missing `git` on PATH: same, doctor reports it; hooks never depended on it.
- **Auth failure**: `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` makes git fail immediately instead of hanging on a prompt (verified: connection refused and missing remote both return 128 at once); the class-specific backoff caps at 15 min, reads continue, doctor shows the last git stderr line (sanitized).
- **Push permission denied (read-only collaborator)** or **namespace rejected**: fallback ladder, then read-only mode; the developer is still informed about teammates and told they are invisible.
- **Force pushes on the team's branches**: irrelevant, our refs are independent orphans. **Someone deletes or mirror-pushes over our refs** (verified E-P): the lease fails or the ref vanishes; the writer re-creates its ref at the next tick, readers see a gap of at most one interval.
- **Host hides the namespace mid-flight** (verified E-N2 pattern): the reader detects that its own ref is missing right after a successful push, flags `transport: "degraded"`, skips the prune and keeps the last snapshot.
- **Shallow clones, worktrees, submodules**: unaffected (shadow repo).
- **Two devices with the same device id** (copied home directory): stale lease → re-list → regenerate `device.json` if the remote tip's manifest carries a different `boot_id`, then push under the new id; the old ref ages out through the janitor.
- **Worker crash or stale lock**: next hook run detects the dead pid and restarts the worker; every write is tmp+rename so a half-written snapshot is never visible.
- **Internal error anywhere**: hooks catch everything, log locally, exit 0 with no output (hooks-core.md L363; prior-art-relay-notes.md L202); the worker catches per tick and continues.
- **Clock skew**: ages are computed writer-side (`generated_at` minus record time) and then offset by reader time since `fetched_at`, so a teammate with a wrong clock cannot make their claims look fresh; timestamps more than 5 min in the future are clamped.
host_compatibility: General (assumption, not verified from this Mac): git hosts accept pushes to ref names outside refs/heads and refs/tags as long as the ref name passes check-ref-format and no server-side rule rejects it; branch protection, required reviews and PR-merge policies are defined on refs/heads/* (and tag rules on refs/tags/*), so refs/synchrobuilder/v1/* is outside their scope on every host I know. That is a design advantage (no PR needed, no CI triggered) and something a security reviewer may want to know about (see security_notes). The write permission required is ordinary push access; readers need only fetch access.

GitHub (assumption from prior art, not verified here): custom namespaces such as refs/notes/*, git-bug's refs/bugs/* and Entire's per-object checkpoint refs (prior-art-relay-notes.md L123) are accepted and advertised in ls-remote; the web UI shows only branches and tags; refs/pull/* is reserved and read-only. Branch rulesets target branches/tags; GitHub's newer 'push rulesets' (file path/extension/size restrictions) may apply to every push regardless of ref, and 'block force pushes' rules apply to branches only. Actions `on: push` should not fire for non-branch/tag refs and push webhooks may or may not fire. All four points are listed under experiments_needed.

GitLab (assumption): custom refs are accepted except reserved namespaces (refs/merge-requests/*, refs/pipelines/*, refs/environments/*, refs/keep-around/*, refs/tmp/*, refs/remotes/*, which gitlab-shell rejects); protected branches apply to refs/heads only; Premium 'push rules' (commit author email must match, reject unsigned commits, commit message regex) are applied to the commits in a push and may therefore apply to our commits too, which is why the commit uses the developer's real name/email and a plain message. Pipelines run for branches/tags only. GitLab.com applies Git-over-HTTP rate limits per user/IP; at one push every 30-60 s per developer this should be far below them, but it is unverified. Hidden from the UI.

Bitbucket Cloud (uncertain): I recall reports that Bitbucket Cloud rejects pushes to refs outside refs/heads and refs/tags; if true, the ladder falls back to refs/heads/synchrobuilder/v1/<h>/<d> branches, which Bitbucket branch permissions can still block or force-push-protect by pattern. Bitbucket Data Center (self-hosted) is generally believed to accept custom refs (it uses refs/pull-requests/* itself). Both need the probe experiment.

Azure DevOps Repos (uncertain): I recall that Azure Repos restricts which ref namespaces can be pushed (refs/heads, refs/tags and a few internal ones) and returns TF-prefixed errors otherwise; if so, branch mode is the only option there, and branch policies configured with a wildcard on synchrobuilder/* would have to be excluded by the repo admin. Needs the probe experiment.

Self-hosted bare repos / Gitea / Forgejo / Gogs / Gerrit: plain git accepts anything (verified with a bare hub); receive.denyNonFastForwards=true blocks the force push but the parented fast-forward chain still works (verified E-I); receive.denyDeletes would stop the janitor (doctor reports it). Gerrit's refs/for/* and refs/changes/* are special, so the namespace must not collide with them (it does not). Gitea/Forgejo show only branches/tags in the UI (assumption).

Fallback branch mode on any host: visible in branch lists (one branch per handle/device), may be caught by wildcard branch protections or 'require PR' rulesets, and force-push blocks turn it into the fast-forward chain with periodic re-root attempts; a repo admin can exclude synchrobuilder/* from such rules. The install page must say so.

Proxies / private CAs / SSO: git uses the developer's existing http.proxy, http.sslCAInfo, credential helpers and SSH agent; nothing extra is configured. Desktop-launched sessions with a minimal PATH or no SSH agent will fail auth fast and land in read-only mode with a doctor message (experiments.md L145 shows how fail-open behaves when node itself is missing; git is the analogous case). `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_PREFER_HTTPS` (monitors-tools-env.md L307) affects plugin installation only, not our transport.
proposals.windows_notes:
- All git invocations are `execFile('git', argv)`: `git.exe` from Git for Windows is a real executable, so no shell and no `.cmd` shim is involved (the same reason exec-form `node` hooks work on Windows: windows-notes.md L64, L293). `git` must be on the PATH of the process that launched Claude Code; `/synchrobuilder:doctor` checks `git --version` and reports the fix. Git for Windows credential flow: Git Credential Manager may open a GUI prompt when no credential is cached; the worker sets `GCM_INTERACTIVE=never` and `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` so it fails fast instead (the GCM variable is an assumption to verify).
- The shadow repo lives under `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\plugins\data\synchrobuilder-<marketplace>\remotes\<key>\git` (windows-notes.md L241); all paths we build use forward slashes and `path.join`, and the repoKey is a hash so long remote URLs never lengthen the path.
- Paths inside claims and journals are stored repo-relative with forward slashes; the PreToolUse and PostToolUse hooks normalize `tool_input.file_path` (backslashes, hooks-events-session-and-pretool.md L299; windows-notes.md L295, L313) and compare case-insensitively on Windows and macOS. The user's top-level path used for `index.json` is taken from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (forward slashes on Windows) and normalized the same way.
- Content bytes: `hash-object --no-filters` plus `core.autocrlf=false` in the shadow repo, so CRLF conversion never touches our JSON; files are written UTF-8 without BOM (windows-notes.md L303).
- Atomic snapshot writes use tmp + `fs.renameSync`; on NTFS a rename over a file another process has open can fail with EPERM/EBUSY (antivirus or a hook mid-read), so the writer retries up to five times with 20 ms sleeps, and readers treat a transient read failure as "no snapshot" (fail open).
- Detached worker: Node's `detached: true` + `windowsHide: true` + `stdio: 'ignore'` + `unref()` is documented for Windows but verified only on macOS (experiments.md L180); `process.kill(pid, 0)` for liveness works on Windows in Node. Both go on the Windows CI list together with the checks already in windows-notes.md L293-L306.
- Case-insensitive filesystem: handles and device ids are lowercase by construction, so loose ref files never collide.
- Shell-launched surfaces (status line command, optional monitor) use forward-slash `node C:/Users/.../x.mjs` strings because Git Bash eats unquoted backslashes (windows-notes.md L192-L221); the transport itself has no shell surface.
proposals.security_notes:
- **Trust boundary = push access to the repo.** Anyone who can push can write any ref, including `refs/synchrobuilder/v1/<someone-else>/...`; that is the same trust model as a shared orphan branch and as the repo's own history. Readers cross-check the tip commit's committer email against `.synchrobuilder/team.json` for the handle and flag mismatches as "unverified writer" in the digest, but that is forgeable. A v2 option is signed commits (`gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile` built from `team.json` keys, `git verify-commit`) with unverified writers demoted to informational only.
- **What leaves the machine** (only via the writer tree): handle, random device id, repo-relative file paths, absolute timestamps, branch name, a derived objective (<=140 chars, from branch/task text, not prompts), claim reasons and notify messages typed by the user (<=200 chars / <=2 KB, passed through a secret-pattern scrub before entering the tree; if Relay's regex list is reused, its MIT notice goes in the file header, prior-art-relay-notes.md L129), task titles, handoff facts derived from tool events (files edited, commits, completed tasks), and contract-change alerts as paths plus a short content hash. Never: prompts, transcripts, source file contents, diff hunks, environment values, hostnames, absolute paths, or the `last_assistant_message` text (handoff lines derived from assistant prose are off by default and require an explicit per-repo opt-in, matching the open question in prior-art-relay-notes.md L205).
- **Untrusted inbound data.** Every blob is parsed with size caps before JSON.parse, validated against a fixed schema, string fields are length-capped and control characters stripped, paths are display-only (never opened or written), timestamps clamped; malformed or oversized writers are ignored and counted in doctor. Text shown to Claude is wrapped in a labeled block with the four peer-message limits (agent-teams-and-cross-session-messaging.md L346) and phrased as facts (hooks-core.md L335); Claude Code adds no marker of its own, so the plugin must.
- **Bypass of review policies.** Because these refs sit outside branch rules, an organization could regard them as an unreviewed data channel in the repo. The write side is limited to the plugin's own small JSON schema, but a repo admin can still forbid the namespace with a pre-receive hook or (on hosts that support it) a push rule; the ladder then degrades to branch mode or read-only, and the install page documents the namespace so admins can allowlist or block it deliberately.
- **No shell anywhere.** Every git call is an argv array through `execFile`, so writer-controlled strings (handles from team.json, messages) are never interpreted by a shell; ref components are regex-restricted and re-checked with `git check-ref-format`.
- **Local files.** `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` is under the user's home; the shadow repo contains only our state; logs contain timings and classified errors, never blob contents or URLs with credentials (the remote URL is stored only in the shadow config that git itself needs; the snapshot stores its hash).
- **Consent.** Setup, the namespace probe (first push), status-line settings and `/synchrobuilder:leave` are explicit commands; the background worker starts automatically only after setup has been completed once for that remote, so an installed-but-not-set-up plugin never pushes anything.
proposals.complexity_estimate: Medium. About 1,500-2,000 lines of dependency-free Node ESM in eight modules: transport interface (~100), git-refs transport with spawn/timeouts/error classification (~400), tree builder and binary tree/blob reader (~250), sync worker with lock, wake watcher, backoff and janitor (~350), fold/merge into snapshot plus staleness ladder (~300), identity/config/remote resolution (~200), snapshot readers used by hooks (~100), doctor checks (~150). Tests: a local bare hub fixture like the one used here, driven from `tests/`, covering force/lease/prune/delete/hidden-namespace/denyNonFastForwards paths (~500 lines). Effort: 2-3 engineer-weeks to a v1 that passes on macOS and Linux against a local hub and GitHub, plus about one week for Windows CI and the host probes (GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps). The hub-later abstraction adds no code now beyond the interface.
risks: Host rejects or hides custom ref namespaces (Bitbucket Cloud and Azure DevOps are the likely cases): mitigated by the probe and the branch-mode fallback, but branch mode is visible in the UI and can collide with wildcard branch rules.

Push cadence: one push per 30-120 s per active developer may trigger push webhooks, CI 'on push' on hosts that do not filter by ref, or Git-over-HTTP rate limits on GitLab.com; mitigated by heartbeat coalescing (2-10 min) and change-only pushes, but unverified.

A teammate's `git push --mirror` (or a repo migration) deletes every synchrobuilder ref (verified locally); self-heals within one tick but causes a brief presence gap and a burst of re-creation pushes.

Detached worker lifecycle is verified only on macOS; on Windows/Linux, or at interactive-session teardown (hooks-async-prompt-security.md L302-L303), the worker might be killed or might linger; the pid-liveness exit rule bounds lingering to two ticks.

Desktop-launched sessions with a minimal PATH or no SSH agent may lack `git` or credentials; the transport goes read-only or local-only and must say so clearly, otherwise users think teammates are absent.

Impersonation and unreviewed content: anyone with push access can write another handle's ref or push arbitrary JSON; the schema validation limits impact but not attribution until signed commits are added.

Repo-local git config not copied into the shadow repo (an unusual `insteadOf` or credential helper set only in the repo) breaks auth silently; mitigated by copying the listed keys and by doctor showing the last git error.
Host-side object growth between gcs (~4 KB per tick per writer) and loose-object churn on hosts that gc rarely; small but nonzero.
Clock skew or a developer with a badly wrong clock producing stale-looking or future claims; clamping plus writer-relative ages mitigate but cannot fully fix.

Namespace-hidden detection relies on the writer's own recent push; a read-only developer cannot distinguish 'everyone left' from 'host hides the namespace' and will show an empty team (doctor can run an explicit ls-remote to help).
Snapshot fold cost grows with N writers (three git spawns, but N trees and N*k blobs to parse); fine to a few hundred writers, untested beyond that.

Two clones of the same repo on one machine with different remote URLs (SSH vs HTTPS) produce two remoteKeys and two workers; normalization of URLs (host, path, .git suffix) must be careful or presence splits.
The 50 ms hook budget depends on Node start-up on the target machine (20 ms measured here, unknown on Windows CI); the snapshot read itself is a single small file.
